3g2.name: 3G2
3g2.summary: A container format defined by 3GPP2 for video on CDMA mobile phones. It is similar to 3GP and based on the MPEG-4 container.
usedFor: Video on older CDMA mobile phones

3gp.name: 3GP
3gp.summary: A container format defined by the 3rd Generation Partnership Project for video on mobile phones. It is a simplified version of the MP4 container and keeps files small.
properties: H.263, H.264 and AAC or AMR audio

aac.name: AAC
aac.summary: A lossy audio codec standardized by MPEG (ISO/IEC 13818-7 and 14496-3) as the successor to MP3. It generally gives better quality than MP3 at the same bitrate.

actionscript.name: ActionScript
actionscript.summary: The programming language of Adobe Flash, an ECMAScript-based language. Flash Player reached end of life at the end of 2020.

ai.name: AI
ai.summary: The native file format of Adobe Illustrator. It stores vector artwork such as paths, shapes, text and effects, and modern files embed a PDF-compatible stream.

aif.name: AIF
aif.summary: A short file extension for AIFF, the Audio Interchange File Format developed by Apple. The data is usually uncompressed PCM audio.

aifc.name: AIFC
aifc.summary: An extension of AIFF that adds support for compressed audio. It uses the same container but can hold compression types such as ULAW or ALAW alongside PCM.

aiff.name: AIFF
aiff.summary: An audio file format developed by Apple in 1988 and based on the IFF container. It usually stores uncompressed PCM audio.

alac.name: ALAC
alac.summary: A lossless audio codec developed by Apple, released as open source in 2011. It is usually stored in an MPEG-4 container with the .m4a extension.
usedFor: Lossless music in the Apple ecosystem

amr.name: AMR
amr.summary: A speech audio codec standardized by 3GPP and widely used in mobile phone networks. It is optimized for voice and compresses to very small files.

apng.name: APNG
apng.summary: An extension of PNG, originally proposed by Mozilla, that stores multiple frames in one file. It keeps PNG's lossless compression and full alpha transparency.

arw.name: ARW
arw.summary: The raw image format of Sony Alpha cameras. It stores unprocessed sensor data, so white balance, exposure and colour can be adjusted later without losing quality.
usedFor: Editing photos before conversion to JPEG

ascii.name: ASCII
ascii.summary: Text that uses only the American Standard Code for Information Interchange character set, 128 characters including letters, digits and punctuation. ASCII is a subset of UTF-8.
usedFor: Text that must work on any system

asciidoc.name: AsciiDoc
asciidoc.summary: A plain-text markup language for writing documentation, articles and books. It can be converted to HTML, PDF and DocBook with tools such as Asciidoctor.

asf.name: ASF
asf.summary: A container format from Microsoft for streaming audio and video. It is the container of WMA and WMV files.

asp.name: ASP
asp.summary: Microsoft's original server-side scripting technology for web pages, released in 1996. Files typically use VBScript and the .asp extension, and it was succeeded by ASP.NET.

au.name: AU
au.summary: A simple audio file format from Sun Microsystems. A short header is followed by audio data, often 8-bit mu-law encoded.

av1.name: AV1
av1.summary: An open, royalty-free video codec released by the Alliance for Open Media in 2018. It compresses more efficiently than VP9 and H.264.
properties: better efficiency than H.264 and VP9

avchd.name: AVCHD
avchd.summary: A format for HD camcorders introduced by Sony and Panasonic in 2006. It records H.264 video in MPEG transport stream files on cards, discs or drives.

avi.name: AVI
avi.summary: A container format introduced by Microsoft in 1992 based on RIFF. It interleaves video and audio data and can hold many different codecs.

avif.name: AVIF
avif.summary: An image format from the Alliance for Open Media that stores AV1-compressed images in the HEIF container. It supports lossy and lossless compression, HDR and transparency.

avro.name: Avro
avro.summary: A row-oriented data serialization format from the Apache Hadoop project. Each file embeds its JSON schema, and data is stored in a compact binary form.

bbcode.name: BBCode
bbcode.summary: A lightweight markup language used in forums and message boards. Tags in square brackets, such as [b] and [url], format text.

bin.name: BIN
bin.summary: A generic extension for files that hold raw binary data. The contents can be an image, a disc image, firmware or an email attachment, so the real type depends on the file.

bmp.name: BMP
bmp.summary: A raster image format introduced with Microsoft Windows that stores pixel data, usually uncompressed. It is simple to read and write but produces large files.

caf.name: CAF
caf.summary: A container format developed by Apple for Core Audio. It has no 4 GB size limit and can hold many audio codecs.

cdda.name: CDDA
cdda.summary: The audio format of audio CDs, defined in the Red Book standard by Philips and Sony. It stores uncompressed 16-bit stereo PCM at 44.1 kHz.

cdr.name: CDR
cdr.summary: The native file format of CorelDRAW, the vector graphics editor from Corel. It stores vector shapes, text, effects and pages.

cr2.name: CR2
cr2.summary: The raw image format used by many Canon EOS cameras from the mid-2000s until CR3 replaced it. It stores unprocessed sensor data in a TIFF-based file.
usedFor: Editing photos before conversion to JPEG

cr3.name: CR3
cr3.summary: The raw image format Canon introduced in 2018 for newer EOS cameras. It uses a container based on the ISO base media file format and can use lossy or lossless compression.
usedFor: Editing photos before conversion to JPEG
properties: ISO base media file format container

crw.name: CRW
crw.summary: The raw image format of early Canon digital cameras, based on the Camera Image File Format (CIFF). Canon replaced it with CR2.
usedFor: Editing photos before conversion to JPEG

csv.name: CSV
csv.summary: A plain-text table format in which each line is a row and values are separated by commas. RFC 4180 describes the common form of the format.

cur.name: CUR
cur.summary: A cursor file format on Microsoft Windows that uses the same structure as ICO, with an added hotspot position that marks the point the pointer clicks.

dax.name: DAX
dax.summary: A formula and query language from Microsoft used in Power BI, Excel Power Pivot and SQL Server Analysis Services to define calculations and tables.
properties: used in Power BI and Power Pivot

dcm.name: DCM
dcm.summary: The file extension for DICOM (Digital Imaging and Communications in Medicine), the standard for storing and exchanging medical images such as X-rays, CT and MRI scans together with patient and study metadata.
properties: image plus patient and study metadata

dds.name: DDS
dds.summary: A Microsoft container format for textures and cubemaps, originally from DirectX. It commonly stores GPU-compressed data in the DXT/BC block formats, with optional mipmaps.

divx.name: DivX
divx.summary: A brand of video codec and container software from DivX, Inc. Early versions were MPEG-4 Part 2 video, usually stored in AVI files, and later versions added H.264.

dng.name: DNG
dng.summary: An open raw image format published by Adobe in 2004 as a single documented alternative to the many proprietary raw formats. It is based on TIFF/EP.
usedFor: Raw files from some phones and cameras

docx.name: DOCX
docx.summary: The default word processing format of Microsoft Word since Word 2007. It is a ZIP package of XML files standardized as Office Open XML (ECMA-376, ISO/IEC 29500).

dot.name: DOT
dot.summary: The template format of Microsoft Word 97 to 2003, using the older binary file format. A template holds styles and layout for new documents.

dss.name: DSS
dss.summary: A compressed speech format developed by Olympus, Philips and Grundig for digital dictation recorders. It is designed for voice rather than music.

dst.name: DST
dst.summary: A machine embroidery stitch file format developed by Tajima. It stores needle positions and commands such as jumps, colour stops and trims rather than a picture.

dv.name: DV
dv.summary: A video format and tape standard for consumer camcorders from the 1990s. It records intraframe-compressed video at about 25 Mbit/s.

dxf.name: DXF
dxf.summary: A CAD data exchange format introduced by Autodesk in 1982 to share drawings between AutoCAD and other programs. It can be stored as text or binary.

emf.name: EMF
emf.summary: A Microsoft vector graphics format that records Windows GDI drawing commands. It is used in Windows and Microsoft Office to embed graphics.
usedFor: Charts and diagrams pasted into Office documents

eps.name: EPS
eps.summary: A file format from Adobe that wraps a PostScript program describing a single page of graphics. It is used to place artwork in other documents.

epub.name: EPUB
epub.summary: An open e-book standard maintained by the W3C (formerly the International Digital Publishing Forum). Content is HTML, CSS and images in a ZIP package, and text reflows to fit the screen.
usedFor: Reading on phones, tablets and e-readers
properties: ZIP package of HTML and CSS

exr.name: EXR
exr.summary: A high-dynamic-range raster format created by Industrial Light & Magic and released as open source in 2003. It stores 16-bit half-float or 32-bit float pixel values.

f4v.name: F4V
f4v.summary: An Adobe Flash video format based on the ISO base media file format (MP4). It holds H.264 video with AAC audio.

firebase.name: Firebase
firebase.summary: JSON data in the shape used by Google's Firebase Realtime Database, which stores data as one large JSON tree. Data can be imported and exported as JSON.

flac.name: FLAC
flac.summary: An open, royalty-free lossless audio codec developed by Xiph.Org. It typically reduces files to about half the size of uncompressed audio while keeping every sample.

flv.name: FLV
flv.summary: A container format created by Macromedia and later Adobe for delivering video through Flash Player. Flash reached end of life in 2020, so FLV is now a legacy format.

gif.name: GIF
gif.summary: A raster image format introduced by CompuServe in 1987. It uses LZW compression, a palette of at most 256 colours per frame, and supports simple animation.

gsm.name: GSM
gsm.summary: A speech codec used in GSM mobile networks, also known as Full Rate. It compresses telephone-quality speech to 13 kbit/s.

hdr.name: HDR
hdr.summary: A high-dynamic-range image format created for the Radiance lighting simulation software, also known as RGBE. It stores each pixel as an RGB mantissa with a shared exponent.

heic.name: HEIC
heic.summary: Apple's name for images stored in the HEIF container with HEVC (H.265) compression. iPhones and iPads have saved photos this way by default since iOS 11.
usedFor: Photos taken on iPhone and iPad
properties: smaller files than JPEG at similar quality
openWith: Windows Photos with the HEIF extension

heif.name: HEIF
heif.summary: A container format standardized by MPEG as ISO/IEC 23008-12 for single images and image sequences, most often compressed with HEVC. HEIC and AVIF files are HEIF variants.
openWith: Windows Photos with the HEIF extension

hevc.name: HEVC
hevc.summary: A video codec standardized as ITU-T H.265 and ISO/IEC 23008-2 in 2013. It compresses about as well as H.264 at roughly half the bitrate.
properties: about 50 percent lower bitrate than H.264

html.name: HTML
html.summary: The standard markup language for web pages, maintained by the WHATWG as the HTML Living Standard. It describes the structure of a page with elements and attributes.

icns.name: ICNS
icns.summary: The icon file format of macOS. A single file holds an icon at several sizes and resolutions, including Retina versions.
usedFor: Folder and document icons on macOS
properties: used by macOS and iOS-derived tooling

ico.name: ICO
ico.summary: A container format for icons on Microsoft Windows that can hold several bitmap images of different sizes and colour depths in a single file. Browsers also use it for favicons.

image.name: Image
image.summary: A general term for a picture file such as JPG, PNG, WebP, GIF or BMP. Converters labelled Image accept several of these common formats as input.
usedFor: Photos and graphics of any common type
properties: accepted types depend on the tool

ini.name: INI
ini.summary: A simple configuration file format of key-value pairs grouped in sections with names in square brackets. It originated in early versions of Windows.

jfif.name: JFIF
jfif.summary: A container convention for JPEG-compressed images that specifies colour space and pixel aspect ratio. Files ending in .jfif contain ordinary JPEG image data.
usedFor: Images saved from some browsers and Windows tools

jif.name: JIF
jif.summary: The original file layout described in the JPEG standard for storing JPEG-compressed images. It was largely superseded by JFIF and Exif, and .jif files are rarely seen.

jira.name: Jira
jira.summary: The text formatting syntax of Atlassian Jira, used for issue descriptions and comments. Tables use pipe characters, with double pipes marking header cells.

jp2.name: JPEG 2000
jp2.summary: A wavelet-based image format standardized as ISO/IEC 15444 by the Joint Photographic Experts Group. It supports lossy and lossless compression in one codestream.

jpg.name: JPG
jpg.summary: A lossy raster image format defined by the Joint Photographic Experts Group (ISO/IEC 10918-1), designed for photographs. .jpg and .jpeg are the same format.

jps.name: JPS
jps.summary: A stereoscopic 3D image format that stores the left and right views side by side in one JPEG file.
usedFor: Images for 3D viewers and VR headsets
properties: left and right views in one image

json.name: JSON
json.summary: A text format for structured data derived from JavaScript syntax. It is standardized as ECMA-404 and RFC 8259, and is the usual format for web APIs.
properties: objects, arrays, strings, numbers and booleans

jsonlines.name: JSON Lines
jsonlines.summary: A text format in which each line is one valid JSON value, usually an object. It lets large datasets be read and written one record at a time.

jxl.name: JPEG XL
jxl.summary: An image format standardized as ISO/IEC 18181 by the Joint Photographic Experts Group. It supports lossy and lossless compression and can losslessly recompress existing JPEG files.

ktx.name: KTX
ktx.summary: A container format from the Khronos Group for GPU textures used with OpenGL and OpenGL ES. It stores texture data together with the information needed to upload it.

ktx2.name: KTX2
ktx2.summary: The second version of the Khronos texture container. It supports Vulkan and other APIs and can carry Basis Universal data that is transcoded to the GPU's native format.

latex.name: LaTeX
latex.summary: A document preparation system built on Donald Knuth's TeX, created by Leslie Lamport. Authors write plain text with commands and compile it into a typeset document.

m2ts.name: M2TS
m2ts.summary: The file extension for video on Blu-ray discs and AVCHD camcorders. It is an MPEG-2 transport stream with a 4-byte timestamp added to each packet.

m2v.name: M2V
m2v.summary: A file extension for a raw MPEG-2 video elementary stream without audio. It is commonly used in DVD authoring.

m4a.name: M4A
m4a.summary: An audio-only file in the MPEG-4 container (MP4). It usually holds AAC audio, or lossless Apple Lossless (ALAC) audio.
usedFor: Music from iTunes and Apple Music

m4b.name: M4B
m4b.summary: An audiobook file in the MPEG-4 container. It is the same as M4A but the extension tells players to remember playback position and supports chapter markers.

m4p.name: M4P
m4p.summary: An MPEG-4 audio file with Apple's FairPlay copy protection, used for songs bought from the early iTunes Store. Files can only be played by authorized Apple software or devices.

m4r.name: M4R
m4r.summary: The file extension for iPhone ringtones. It is an MPEG-4 audio file with AAC audio, renamed so iTunes and the iPhone treat it as a ringtone.

m4v.name: M4V
m4v.summary: A video file format developed by Apple that is very close to MP4. Files from the iTunes Store may be protected with FairPlay DRM.
usedFor: Videos in iTunes and Apple TV

mac.name: MAC
mac.summary: The image format of MacPaint, the drawing program released with the original Apple Macintosh in 1984. Images are 576 by 720 pixels, black and white, and packed with PackBits.

markdown.name: Markdown
markdown.summary: A lightweight markup language created by John Gruber in 2004. Plain text with simple symbols for headings, lists, links and emphasis converts to HTML.

matlab.name: MATLAB
matlab.summary: MATLAB is the numerical computing environment and language from MathWorks, in which matrices and arrays are the core data types.

mediawiki.name: MediaWiki
mediawiki.summary: The wikitext markup used by MediaWiki, the software behind Wikipedia. It defines headings, links, lists and tables with plain-text symbols.

mjpeg.name: MJPEG
mjpeg.summary: A video codec that compresses each frame as a separate JPEG image. It does not use compression between frames, so every frame can be edited alone.
properties: easy to edit frame by frame

mkv.name: MKV
mkv.summary: An open, free container format that can hold unlimited video, audio, picture and subtitle tracks in one file. WebM is a subset of Matroska.
usedFor: Videos with multiple audio and subtitle tracks

mov.name: MOV
mov.summary: The container format of Apple's QuickTime, which also served as the basis for the MPEG-4 file format. It stores video, audio, text and timecode tracks.

mp2.name: MP2
mp2.summary: A lossy audio format standardized by MPEG, defined as Layer II of MPEG-1 Audio. It is used in digital radio, DVD-Video and broadcast television.

mp3.name: MP3
mp3.summary: A lossy audio format standardized by MPEG (ISO/IEC 11172-3), developed with major contributions from the Fraunhofer Society. It became the most common format for downloadable music.

mp4.name: MP4
mp4.summary: A container format defined in ISO/IEC 14496-14 that can hold video, audio, subtitles and metadata. H.264 video with AAC audio is the most common combination.

mpeg2.name: MPEG-2
mpeg2.summary: A video and audio coding standard from MPEG (ISO/IEC 13818, ITU-T H.262). It is used for DVD-Video, digital television and broadcast.

mpg.name: MPG
mpg.summary: A file extension for MPEG-1 or MPEG-2 video and audio in an MPEG program stream. It was the standard for VCD and DVD video.

mpv.name: MPV
mpv.summary: A file extension for an MPEG video elementary stream, typically MPEG-1 or MPEG-2 video without audio.

mts.name: MTS
mts.summary: The file extension for video recorded by AVCHD camcorders. It is an MPEG transport stream containing H.264 video.
usedFor: HD video from Sony and Panasonic cameras

mxf.name: MXF
mxf.summary: A container format standardized by SMPTE (SMPTE 377M) for professional video and audio. It carries essence data together with timecode and metadata.

mysql.name: MySQL
mysql.summary: SQL statements in the MySQL dialect, such as those produced by mysqldump. MySQL is an open-source relational database owned by Oracle.

nef.name: NEF
nef.summary: The raw image format of Nikon digital cameras. It stores unprocessed sensor data in a TIFF-based file, with an embedded JPEG preview.
usedFor: Editing photos before conversion to JPEG

oga.name: OGA
oga.summary: The Ogg container extension recommended for audio-only files. It can hold Vorbis, FLAC or Opus audio.

ogg.name: OGG
ogg.summary: A free container format maintained by Xiph.Org. The .ogg extension is most commonly used for Vorbis audio, a lossy codec.

ogv.name: OGV
ogv.summary: The Ogg container extension for video files. It usually holds Theora video with Vorbis or Opus audio.
usedFor: Web video in Firefox and Chrome

opus.name: Opus
opus.summary: An open lossy audio codec standardized by the IETF in RFC 6716. It works well for both speech and music and for low-delay use.

orf.name: ORF
orf.summary: The raw image format of Olympus digital cameras, now OM System. It stores unprocessed sensor data in a TIFF-based file.
usedFor: Photography with Olympus and OM System cameras
Editing photos before conversion to JPEG

otf.name: OTF
otf.summary: A font format developed by Microsoft and Adobe, standardized as ISO/IEC 14496-22. OTF files usually contain PostScript-style (CFF) outlines and support advanced typographic features.

pam.name: PAM
pam.summary: A Netpbm format that generalizes PBM, PGM and PPM. It adds a header describing the number of channels, so it can carry an alpha channel.

pandasdataframe.name: Pandas DataFrame
pandasdataframe.summary: A two-dimensional table of labelled rows and columns from pandas, the data analysis library for Python. It is the standard structure for tabular data in Python.

pbm.name: PBM
pbm.summary: The black-and-white member of the Netpbm family of formats. Each pixel is one bit, and files can be stored as plain text or in a binary form.

pcd.name: PCD
pcd.summary: The image format of Kodak's Photo CD system, introduced in 1992. Each file holds one photo at several resolutions, from thumbnail to high resolution.
usedFor: Photos scanned to Photo CD discs

pcx.name: PCX
pcx.summary: A raster image format created by ZSoft for the PC Paintbrush program in the 1980s. It uses run-length encoding and was widely used on DOS and early Windows.

pdf.name: PDF
pdf.summary: A document format created by Adobe in 1993 and standardized as ISO 32000. It keeps text, fonts, images and layout the same on any device.
usedFor: Sharing documents that must look the same everywhere

pes.name: PES
pes.summary: A machine embroidery file format created by Brother and used by Brother and Babylock machines. It stores stitch data, thread colours and a design preview.

pgm.name: PGM
pgm.summary: The greyscale member of the Netpbm family of formats. Each pixel is a grey value, stored as plain text or in a binary form.

php.name: PHP
php.summary: A general-purpose scripting language created by Rasmus Lerdorf in 1994, designed mainly for web development. It powers WordPress and many other web applications.

png.name: PNG
png.summary: A lossless raster image format developed in the mid-1990s as a patent-free replacement for GIF and standardized as ISO/IEC 15948 and a W3C Recommendation.
usedFor: Web graphics that must stay sharp

ppm.name: PPM
ppm.summary: The colour member of the Netpbm family of formats. Each pixel stores red, green and blue values, in a plain text or binary encoding.

ppt.name: PPT
ppt.summary: The binary presentation format of Microsoft PowerPoint from PowerPoint 97 to 2003. It was replaced by PPTX in PowerPoint 2007.
usedFor: Presentations shared with older PowerPoint versions

pptx.name: PPTX
pptx.summary: The default presentation format of Microsoft PowerPoint since PowerPoint 2007. It is a ZIP package of XML files standardized as Office Open XML (ECMA-376, ISO/IEC 29500).

protobuf.name: Protobuf
protobuf.summary: A language-neutral binary serialization format developed by Google. Data structures are defined in .proto files, and code is generated for many programming languages.

psd.name: PSD
psd.summary: The native file format of Adobe Photoshop. It stores layers, masks, adjustment layers, text and colour information so a design can be edited later.

qlik.name: Qlik
qlik.summary: Data prepared for Qlik, the business intelligence platform that includes Qlik Sense. Data is loaded into Qlik apps with a load script.
properties: used in Qlik Sense and QlikView

qt.name: QT
qt.summary: An alternative file extension for Apple's QuickTime movie container, which is the same format as MOV.

ra.name: RA
ra.summary: An audio format from RealNetworks, introduced in 1995 for streaming over the internet. It is now a legacy format.
usedFor: Old internet radio and streaming archives

raf.name: RAF
raf.summary: The raw image format of Fujifilm digital cameras. It stores unprocessed sensor data together with an embedded JPEG preview.
usedFor: Editing photos before conversion to JPEG

rdataframe.name: R data frame
rdataframe.summary: The standard table structure of the R language, with named columns that can hold different types of data. It is built into R.
usedFor: Loading tabular data into R scripts

rdf.name: RDF
rdf.summary: A W3C standard model for describing resources as subject, predicate, object triples. It can be written in several syntaxes, such as RDF/XML, Turtle and JSON-LD.
usedFor: Linked data and the semantic web

restructuredtext.name: reStructuredText
restructuredtext.summary: A plain-text markup language from the Python Docutils project. It is the default format of Sphinx documentation and Python docstrings.

rgb.name: RGB
rgb.summary: A raster image format from Silicon Graphics, also called SGI image and often using the extensions .sgi, .rgb or .bw. It can use run-length encoding.

rm.name: RM
rm.summary: A multimedia container from RealNetworks, introduced in 1997 for streaming audio and video over the internet. It is now a legacy format.

rmvb.name: RMVB
rmvb.summary: A variant of the RealMedia container that uses variable bitrate encoding. It was popular for sharing movies in the early 2000s.

ruby.name: Ruby
ruby.summary: A dynamic programming language created by Yukihiro Matsumoto and first released in 1995. It is known for the web framework Ruby on Rails.

rw2.name: RW2
rw2.summary: The raw image format of Panasonic Lumix cameras. It stores unprocessed sensor data, and the .rw2 extension is also used by some Leica cameras built with Panasonic.
usedFor: Editing photos before conversion to JPEG

sfw.name: SFW
sfw.summary: A proprietary image format used by Seattle FilmWorks, a mail-order film developer that delivered scans on disk and online in the 1990s. Files are JPEG-based with a modified header.

sql.name: SQL
sql.summary: The standard language for querying and managing relational databases, standardized as ISO/IEC 9075. .sql files hold statements such as CREATE TABLE and INSERT.

svg.name: SVG
svg.summary: An XML-based vector image format and W3C standard. Shapes, paths and text are described mathematically, so images scale to any size without losing sharpness.
usedFor: Logos and icons on the web

swf.name: SWF
swf.summary: A file format for Adobe Flash animations, games and interactive content, originally from Macromedia. Flash Player reached end of life on 31 December 2020.

textile.name: Textile
textile.summary: A lightweight markup language created by Dean Allen in 2002 that converts plain text into HTML. It is used by some content management systems and issue trackers.
usedFor: Content in some CMS and wikis
properties: short syntax for tables and lists

tga.name: TGA
tga.summary: A raster image format introduced by Truevision in 1984. It stores 8 to 32 bits per pixel with optional run-length encoding and an alpha channel.

tiff.name: TIFF
tiff.summary: A flexible raster image format first published by Aldus in 1986 and now maintained by Adobe. It stores one or more images with a tag-based structure and many compression options.

toml.name: TOML
toml.summary: A configuration file format created by Tom Preston-Werner. It maps clearly to a hash table and uses key-value pairs grouped in sections.

tracwiki.name: Trac Wiki
tracwiki.summary: The wiki markup used by Trac, the open-source project management and bug tracking tool. It describes headings, lists, links and tables in plain text.

ts.name: TS
ts.summary: A container format standardized in MPEG-2 Systems (ISO/IEC 13818-1) for broadcasting. It splits video, audio and data into small fixed-size packets so streams survive transmission errors.

ttf.name: TTF
ttf.summary: An outline font format developed by Apple and licensed to Microsoft in the late 1980s. It is supported by Windows, macOS, Linux and web browsers.

txt.name: TXT
txt.summary: A file that holds unformatted text with no fonts, styles or images. It is readable by any text editor, on any operating system.

vob.name: VOB
vob.summary: The container used for video, audio, subtitles and menus on DVD-Video discs. It is based on the MPEG-2 program stream.

wav.name: WAV
wav.summary: An audio container format developed by Microsoft and IBM that is based on RIFF. It usually holds uncompressed PCM audio, so files are large but exact.

wbmp.name: WBMP
wbmp.summary: A monochrome image format defined in the WAP (Wireless Application Protocol) specifications for early mobile phones. Each pixel is a single bit.

webm.name: WebM
webm.summary: An open media format designed for the web, based on a subset of Matroska. It carries VP8, VP9 or AV1 video with Vorbis or Opus audio.

webp.name: WebP
webp.summary: An image format developed by Google, first released in 2010 and built on the VP8 video codec for lossy images. It also supports lossless compression, transparency and animation.

wma.name: WMA
wma.summary: A family of audio codecs developed by Microsoft and stored in the ASF container. The standard version is lossy, and a WMA Lossless variant exists.

wmv.name: WMV
wmv.summary: A family of video codecs developed by Microsoft, usually stored in the ASF container. It was widely used for Windows video and streaming.

wpg.name: WPG
wpg.summary: The graphics format of the WordPerfect word processor. A file can contain vector drawing objects or bitmap data.

wtv.name: WTV
wtv.summary: The file format used by Windows Media Center to record television, starting with Windows Vista and replacing DVR-MS. It stores broadcast video, audio and metadata.
usedFor: TV recordings from Windows Media Center

xbm.name: XBM
xbm.summary: A monochrome image format of the X Window System. The image is stored as C source code, an array of bytes that can be compiled into a program.
usedFor: Cursors and icons in X11 programs

xcf.name: XCF
xcf.summary: The native file format of GIMP, the GNU Image Manipulation Program. It keeps layers, channels, paths and selections so an image can be edited again.

xls.name: XLS
xls.summary: The binary workbook format of Microsoft Excel from Excel 97 to Excel 2003. It was replaced by XLSX in Excel 2007.
usedFor: Workbooks shared with older Excel versions
properties: maximum 65,536 rows and 256 columns per sheet

xlsx.name: XLSX
xlsx.summary: The default workbook format of Microsoft Excel since Excel 2007. It is a ZIP package of XML files standardized as Office Open XML (ECMA-376, ISO/IEC 29500).
properties: over one million rows per sheet

xml.name: XML
xml.summary: A markup language for structured data, maintained by the W3C. Custom tags describe the data, and both people and programs can read it.

xpm.name: XPM
xpm.summary: A colour image format of the X Window System. Like XBM, it is stored as C source code, with a colour table and one character per pixel.

xps.name: XPS
xps.summary: A fixed-layout document format developed by Microsoft and standardized as ECMA-388. It is a ZIP package of XML pages, similar in purpose to PDF.

yaml.name: YAML
yaml.summary: A human-readable data format that uses indentation to show structure. It is widely used for configuration files and is a superset of JSON from version 1.2.
